conviction_note: The fundamentals lean mildly good: the Q3 EPS bar is $0.04 and revenue consensus is stale at $21.5-22.5M against Q2's $29.0M, and Q4 tanker rates are extreme. The tape leans clearly the other way: +57% in three sessions (0.93 to 1.46) on no news in a 6.0M-share float, and the last three prints were all sold, including a May setup that went +29% into the print and then -20%. So p_up is 35 on an abs move of 15 (thin float, 152% realised vol, no options). That gives -4.5 against a findings sum of -6.1. The sum is larger because the two tape findings are sized at full size while the scaled number carries the risk that the Q4 rate commentary extends the squeeze.

findings.finding: HMR rose 57% in three sessions into the print, from 0.93 (Nov 23) to 1.46 (Nov 27 half-day close: +15.05%, +13.08%, +20.66%). The Nov 27 half-day traded 583k shares, about 10% of the 6.04M float. There was no company release or SEC filing after Sep 9, and Tickeron found no company catalyst (sector backdrop only, 'news significance 30/100'). So the stock enters a bmo print with a speculative premium on a stock that was 0.93 four sessions ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026, the closest analog: 1.16 to 1.50 (+29%) on May 22 into the May 26 Q1 release, 1.57 on May 26, then 1.25 on May 27 (-20.4%) and 1.14 on May 28 (Yahoo chart bars). The run built before the print and unwound within two sessions.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, not a fact the price missed. The question is whether the premium survives the release. If the market had already discounted a sell-the-news unwind, the stock would not have closed at the high of the run on the heaviest volume in a month. Nothing explains the run (no 6-K, no fleet release, no filing on EDGAR since Sep 9), so it has to be validated by the release or unwind.
findings.independence: The Tickeron blog (https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-heidmar-maritime-holdings-corp-hmr-stock-up-15-70-today-48436/, 2026-11-27) confirms the Nov 27 move had no company catalyst and cites a ~6M float. EDGAR's filing list (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002029471) shows nothing after 2026-09-09. This finding and the reaction-history finding both point to sell-the-news, but they rest on different data (this run vs prior prints).

findings.finding: The last three prints were all sold on release. Q4 2025 (Mar 24, 2026): 0.902 to 0.856, -5.1%, then -4.6% the next day. Q1 2026 (May 26): +4.7% on the day after a +29% pre-print spike, then -20.4% on May 27. Q2 2026 (Sep 1, bmo): 1.39 to 1.24, -10.8%. The Q2 sell-off came despite revenue of $29.0M against a ~$21.4-24.4M consensus and bullish rate commentary.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: three of three prints in 2026 closed lower within two sessions. The Q2 revenue beat with an EPS miss against a disputed $0.10 bar was sold -10.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline carries no reaction history: the 6-K archive was unread, so n=0. A market that had priced this pattern would not bid the stock 57% into the release. The reaction function exists only in the daily bars, which no aggregator summarises for this name.
findings.independence: The Q2 reaction is independently reported as 'Heidmar Maritime Stock Down 10.8%' (dailypolitical aggregator snippet, https://www.dailypolitical.com/?p=10489932, 403 to fetch). Release dates come from https://www.heidmar.com/news/. The pre-print-spike pattern overlaps conceptually with the run-up finding but uses different data.

findings.finding: Q3 EPS should come in at or above the $0.04 bar, and revenue should clear the stale $21.5-22.5M consensus. Q2 revenue was $29.0M: trade revenues $5.80M plus voyage/time-charter $23.20M. Q3 adds Q-Shipping management fees (nine managed vessels from Jul 1, three more taken over in Q3) on a ~60-vessel commercially managed fleet. Q2 G&A of $5.57M included $1.8M of cash bonuses, against Q1 G&A of about $3.56M. If Q3 G&A normalises, operating income gains about $1.5M on a Q2 base of $1.82M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue beat (29.0 vs ~21.4-24.4M) came with an EPS miss against a disputed bar and was sold -10.8%. This name has not paid for revenue beats.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue consensus ($21.5-22.5M) sits 25% below the last actual, which suggests the 2-3 estimates have not been rebuilt for the relet business and Q-Shipping. The EPS bar rests on snippets only, and the prior-quarter bar was disputed (EW $0.10 vs Quiver $0.05), so the size is capped small.
findings.independence: Q-Shipping completion and the nine-vessel addition are confirmed separately by https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/heidmar-maritime-holdings-corp-expands-ship-management-platform-2026-07-07 (2026-07-07). The G&A bonus timing is from the same Q2 PDF, not independent.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Heidmar last spoke show Q4 2026 mid-size tanker bookings at extremes: Teekay Tankers has 58% of Q4 Suezmax spot days at $272,000/day and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300, against Q3 averages of $106,437 and $67,552; DHT has 50% of Q4 VLCC spot days at $509,100. Heidmar runs Suezmax/Aframax pools and earns commissions on pool gross, and in September it guided that 'rates to remain elevated and potentially strengthen further' in Q4/Q1. The Nov 30 call is the first time it can quantify Q4 pool earnings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (Sep 1) carried similar bullish rate commentary ('Suezmaxes in the Mediterranean / Black Sea are at historical highs') and the stock fell -10.8%. Forward commentary has not been paid for at this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Peer rates have been public since Oct 12 (DHT) and Nov 12 (Teekay), yet HMR fell from 1.91 to 0.93 over the same period, so the market has not mapped tanker rates onto HMR's commission line. A Heidmar-specific Q4 pool figure on the call would be new. This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has confirmed only qualitatively, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: DHT Q4 bookings: https://finviz.com/news/401131/dht-holdings-reports-q3-fleet-earnings-of-141300-per-day-as-fourth-quarter-tanker-rates-rise (2026-10-12). Company's own Q4 expectation: Q2 PDF p.3 (2026-09-01).

findings.finding: Q3 realised mid-size spot rates fell slightly from Q2 at the closest listed peer: Teekay Suezmax $106,437 vs $109,171 (-2.5%), Aframax/LR2 $67,552 vs $74,149 (-8.9%). Heidmar's Q3 pool commissions and relet margins (Q2: voyage/TC revenue $23.2M against charter-in and other $21.4M) therefore have no rate tailwind quarter on quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HMR-specific history of reacting to rate-driven misses. Prior prints were sold regardless of the rate backdrop.
findings.why_not_priced: A peer proxy for the Q3 line. Its scale is offset by fleet growth (finding 3), so it is small. The Clarksons index reportedly showed record Q3 Suezmax averages, which points the other way and could not be verified (see rejected).
findings.independence: Shares the Teekay article with the Q4 finding. This finding reads the Q3 line, the other the Q4 bookings; they are separate lines from one document, sized apart.

findings.finding: Heidmar has a $20M committed equity purchase facility with B. Riley Principal Capital II, under which up to 11,080,332 shares are registered for resale. The POS AM went effective June 10, 2026, and the facility runs 36 months. The company can sell shares at its discretion into a spike, and BRPC II resells them. Against a 6.04M float this is a supply overhang on a +57% run. The company has no visible need for the money: $28.7M cash, positive operating cash flow of $7.7M in H1, an asset-light model, and no acquisition named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no disclosed draw. Weighted basic shares rose only from 58.24M (Q2'25) to 59.59M (Q2'26), so usage looks minimal so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility is public, but the share count moving on the Q3 balance sheet or in the subsequent-events note would be new. Asked what the money buys: nothing corroborated, but the company is not in distress either, so the negative is small and rests on supply, not solvency.
findings.independence: EDGAR EFFECT notice dated 2026-06-10 (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0002029471). Same underlying facility.

findings.finding: Director Andreas Konialidis stepped down on Oct 13, 2026, with 'no disagreement'. The company said it would search for a replacement 'in due course'. This is the only company release between the Q2 print and the Q3 date notice.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for six weeks. It matters only if the call names a replacement or ties the departure to a holder exit.

baseline_tension: There is no skew and no reaction history in the baseline. The +44.6% 5-day run-up is the dominant fact, and my negative lean agrees with fading it. That agreement makes the negative partly a bet that the run-up is speculative froth, which the extreme Q4 tanker rates could validate on the call. That risk is why p_up is 35 and not lower.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (an unexplained move is not evidence): run-up finding cut from -6.0 to -4.5. It stays because it rests on the tape plus a dated company analog (May), not on the absence of a cause alone.
Lessons 6 and 1 (bar only from snippets, prior bar disputed, beats sold at this name): Q3 beat finding cut from +1.5 to +0.8.
Lesson 5 (macro-to-company transmission confirmed only qualitatively by the company): Q4 rate guidance finding cut from +2.0 to +1.5.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): asked what the B. Riley equity line buys. The answer was no corroborated use and no distress, so it stays at -0.5 as a supply overhang.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (0.27% of float, 0.14 days), so no squeeze shrink applied to the negatives.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage): abs_move_pct kept at 15 (above one day of 20d vol, 9.6%) rather than shrunk. p_up unchanged at 35.
